relations.rationale: If Yara is in the same class as Milo, and Milo's class relation to Zeno is implied elsewhere, being in the same class as Milo makes 'Yara not in same class as Zeno' less likely unless Milo differs from Zeno; taken alone, sameness with Milo suggests likely sameness with Zeno if Milo=Zeno, contradicting claim 19.
Yara's class relation to Milo has no bearing on when Zeno joined the choir.
Milo and Zeno being in the same class has no connection to a pianist rehearsing opening bars.

If Milo is in the same class as Zeno, and Yara is in the same class as Milo (from other claims), this would contradict Yara not being in the same class as Zeno, but judged alone, Milo-Zeno sameness doesn't directly address Yara-Zeno.
Being in the same class as Zeno has no bearing on how long Zeno has been in the choir.
Milo being in the same class as Zeno doesn't inform how long Milo has been singing with the group.
A pianist repeating opening bars doesn't directly relate to sopranos' pitch struggles in a different measure.
Sopranos struggling with pitch has no bearing on Milo's tenure with the group.
Sopranos' pitch issues during rehearsal don't relate to Hugo stacking chairs afterward.
Yara's class relation to Zeno has no bearing on Hugo's chair-stacking activity.
Yara not being in the same class as Zeno doesn't relate to when the next rehearsal is scheduled.
Zeno joining a year ago versus Milo singing since childhood are independent facts about different people, though both describe tenure, they don't affect each other's likelihood.
Zeno's choir tenure has no bearing on Kai offering to lock up.
Hugo helping with chairs as rehearsal ends is consistent with and supports the scenario of Kai also helping close up afterward.
Hugo helping stack chairs as rehearsal ends doesn't inform whether the next rehearsal is already scheduled.
Kai offering to lock up after everyone leaves doesn't relate to whether the next rehearsal is already scheduled.
